Tithonus grows older and weaker year after year, unable to die, until he is only a shrunken voice.

text: A daughter asks the hospital to keep her father alive by every means possible and signs the order. The doctors do exactly that, but she never asks them to consider whether he could ever wake. For eight years he lies on machines in a coma, wasting away, kept alive and nothing more.
segs: A daughter asks the hospital to keep her father alive by every means possible and signs the order.
The doctors do exactly that, but she never asks them to consider whether he could ever wake.
For eight years he lies on machines in a coma, wasting away, kept alive and nothing more.

text: A daughter asks the hospital to keep her father alive by every means possible and signs the order. The doctors do exactly that, and she also asks them to stop if he could never wake. After two weeks the scans show he never will, so the machines are turned off and he dies with her beside him.
segs: A daughter asks the hospital to keep her father alive by every means possible and signs the order.

text: The dawn goddess Eos loves the mortal Tithonus and carries him off to her palace in the east. The jealous war god Ares hunts him down and wounds him with a spear, and Eos leaves the sky dark for a whole day to nurse him back to health while the frightened world waits for morning.
segs: The dawn goddess Eos loves the mortal Tithonus and carries him off to her palace in the east.
The jealous war god Ares hunts him down and wounds him with a spear,
and Eos leaves the sky dark for a whole day to nurse him back to health while the frightened world waits for morning.

text: The North Wind and the Sun argue over who is stronger and agree that whoever makes a traveler take off his cloak wins. The harder the Wind blows, the tighter the man wraps his cloak around him. Then the Sun shines warmly, and he takes it off himself.
segs: The North Wind and the Sun argue over who is stronger and agree that whoever makes a traveler take off his cloak wins.

the tighter the man wraps his cloak around him. Then the Sun shines warmly, and he takes it off himself.

text: Two managers bet on who can get a stubborn engineer to switch to a new tool. The first sends daily orders and threatens his bonus, and the engineer digs in and clings to his old tools. The second asks his advice on the new tool and praises his ideas, and within a week he switches on his own.

text: Two managers bet on who can get a stubborn engineer to switch to a new tool. text: The North Wind and the Sun argue over who is stronger and fight for the sky all spring, one sending icy gales, the other scorching heat. The crops wither and the farmers despair, and while the two are busy with each other, the Clouds drift in, take over the sky and bring rain, and the farmers honor the Clouds above them both.

text: Procrustes, a robber on the road to Athens, offers travelers a bed for the night. If a guest is too short for his iron bed he stretches him, and if too tall he cuts off his legs. Theseus finally makes Procrustes lie on his own bed and cuts him to fit.

text: A hospital director orders that every patient stay exactly five days. Patients who need longer are sent home sick, and those who recover sooner are kept in beds they do not need. When the director himself breaks his hip, his deputy applies the rule, and he is sent home on day five, still unable to walk.
segs: A hospital director orders that every patient stay exactly five days. Patients who need longer are sent home sick,

text: A hospital director lets doctors decide how long every patient should stay. Patients who need longer are kept longer, and those who recover sooner are sent home early, freeing beds they do not need. When the director himself breaks his hip, a flu outbreak fills every ward, and he is sent home on day five, still unable to walk.

When the director himself breaks his hip, a flu outbreak fills every ward, and he is sent home on day five, still unable to walk.

text: Procrustes, a robber on the road to Athens, drugs travelers' wine and robs them as they sleep in his iron bed. text: Zeus and Hermes, disguised as poor travelers, knock at every door in a rich town and are turned away. Only Baucis and Philemon, an old couple in a tiny cottage, take them in and share their last food. The gods drown the town in a flood and turn the cottage into a temple.

text: A woman in worn clothes asks every big car dealer about a fleet of vans and is ignored. At a small family garage, the old owner makes her coffee and helps her all afternoon. text: Baucis and Philemon, a poor old couple, quarrel over their only goose: he wants to sell it, she wants to keep it. text: Heracles fights the Hydra, a serpent with many heads. Every time he cuts one off, two grow back in its place. His nephew Iolaus brings a torch and burns each neck as soon as the head falls, so nothing can grow back, and the beast is killed.

text: A school bans one gossip site about its students, and within days two new ones appear. Each time a site is shut down, more spring up to replace it. A young IT worker blocks the free service that all of them are built on, so no new sites can be made, and within a month they are gone for good.

text: Heracles fights the Hydra in its swamp. The beast wraps him in its coils, and his nephew Iolaus, who was meant to guard his back, panics and runs away. Heracles fights on alone and kills the beast, but he is badly bitten and must be carried home on a cart, and for the rest of his life he refuses to speak to Iolaus.

text: King Augeas's stables hold thousands of cattle and have not been cleaned in thirty years. Heracles is told to clean them in a single day. Instead of shoveling, he breaks holes in the walls and turns two rivers through the yard, and the water washes the filth away.

text: A city must clear years of built-up silt from its harbor within a week, far more than its dredging boats could ever move. text: King Croesus of Lydia asks the oracle at Delphi whether he should attack Persia. The oracle answers that if he crosses the river, a great empire will fall. Sure of victory, he crosses and attacks, and the great empire that falls is his own.

text: King Croesus of Lydia shows a visiting Athenian his treasure and asks who is the happiest man alive. The guest names a poor farmer who died with honor. text: King Erysichthon cuts down the sacred grove of the goddess Demeter to build a banquet hall, felling her great oak himself. She strikes him with a hunger no food can fill. He eats through all his wealth, sells his own daughter for food, and at last devours his own body.

text: A developer illegally bulldozes a protected forest to build a casino resort. He starts gambling at his own tables and can never stop, however much he wins. text: King Erysichthon orders Demeter's sacred grove cut down to build a banquet hall. His daughter begs him to spare it, and when he refuses she leads the villagers to stand among the trees. segs: Odin, dressed as a ragged traveler on his way home from Mimir's well,
asks a proud king for a drink and a seat by the fire. The king has him tied between two fires for eight nights.
The king's young son secretly brings him a horn of ale, and Odin makes the boy king in his father's place.

text: The gods fear the growing wolf Fenrir and want to bind him with a magic ribbon. Fenrir agrees to be tied only if one god puts a hand in his mouth as a pledge of good faith. Tyr does, the ribbon holds, and the wolf bites off his hand.
segs: The gods fear the growing wolf Fenrir and want to bind him with a magic ribbon.

Tyr does, the ribbon holds, and the wolf bites off his hand.

text: A firm wants a dangerous rival to sign a merger that will quietly shut the rival down. Its owner will sign only if the firm's most trusted negotiator stakes her name on the deal being fair. She knows the plan and gives her word anyway. The deal goes through, the truth comes out, and no one will ever trust her again.
segs: A firm wants a dangerous rival to sign a merger that will quietly shut the rival down.

She knows the plan and gives her word anyway. The deal goes through, the truth comes out, and no one will ever trust her again.

text: The gods raise the wolf Fenrir from a pup, and Tyr alone dares to feed him. When the wolf grows huge and breaks his chains, he does not harm the gods who raised him; he turns on the frost giants attacking their hall one dark winter night, drives them all the way back to their mountains, and lies down again at Tyr's feet.

text: Thor visits the giant Utgard-Loki and fails every contest: he cannot drain a drinking horn, lift a cat, or beat an old nurse at wrestling. He leaves ashamed. Then his host admits the horn was joined to the sea, the cat was the world serpent, and the old woman was old age.

text: A junior chemist is asked to fix three lab samples and fails with all three. She resigns, embarrassed. Then her supervisor tells her the samples were tests no one had ever passed: the first had no fix, the second was a fake, and the third was spoiled on purpose. Her notes come closer than anyone's.

text: Thor visits the giant Utgard-Loki and wins every contest in his hall. The giant, shamed in front of all his guests, pretends to honor Thor with a feast but poisons his mead, and Thor, sick for a whole year, comes back with an army of his own and burns the hall to the ground.

text: The dwarf Alberich's gold and ring are taken from him by force, and he curses them to bring death to whoever owns them. The giant Fafner kills his own brother to keep the hoard; the hero Siegfried kills Fafner and takes it; then Siegfried himself is murdered.

text: A miner's huge uncut diamond is stolen, and he vows that it will bring its owners nothing but grief. The thief is shot by his partner, who wants it all. The partner sells it to a dealer and is arrested within the year. The dealer is robbed and killed, and his heir is ruined by lawsuits over it.

text: A miner's huge uncut diamond is stolen, and he vows that it will bring its owners nothing but grief. The thief sells it to his partner at a fair price. text: The dwarf Alberich forges a ring from gold stolen from the Rhine and grows proud of its power. The gods visit his cave and dare him to show off his magic by turning himself into a toad. He does, they catch him under a foot, and they take the ring and gold as his ransom.

text: A miller boasts that his daughter can spin straw into gold, and the king locks her in a room full of straw. A little man spins it for her in return for her firstborn child. When he comes to collect, he says she may keep the child if she can guess his name, and she does.

text: Six blind men meet an elephant for the first time. One touches its side and says it is a wall, one its trunk and says a snake, one its leg and says a tree, one its ear and says a fan. They argue fiercely, each partly right and all of them wrong.
segs: Six blind men meet an elephant for the first time. One touches its side and says it is a wall,
one its trunk and says a snake, one its leg and says a tree,
one its ear and says a fan. They argue fiercely, each partly right and all of them wrong.

text: Revenue is falling, and four department heads each study only their own reports. Sales blames high prices, support says the product breaks too often, marketing says nobody has heard of it, and delivery blames slow shipping. They fight about it for months, and none of them sees that all four are real.
segs: Revenue is falling, and four department heads each study only their own reports. Sales blames high prices,
support says the product breaks too often, marketing says nobody has heard of it,
and delivery blames slow shipping. They fight about it for months, and none of them sees that all four are real.

text: Revenue is falling, and four department heads study all their reports together. Sales points to high prices, support says the product breaks too often, marketing says nobody has heard of it, and delivery adds slow shipping. They agree that all four are real, fix them one by one, and within a year revenue is climbing again.
segs: Revenue is falling, and four department heads study all their reports together. Sales points to high prices,
support says the product breaks too often, marketing says nobody has heard of it, and delivery adds slow shipping.

text: Six blind men travel to the city to see the king's elephant in the spring parade. A firework scares the animal, and it charges through the crowd. Two of the blind men, who cannot tell which way to run, are knocked down and badly hurt, and the parade is called off for the rest of the year.
segs: Six blind men travel to the city to see the king's elephant in the spring parade.
A firework scares the animal, and it charges through the crowd. Two of the blind men, who cannot tell which way to run,
are knocked down and badly hurt, and the parade is called off for the rest of the year.

text: Brer Fox catches Brer Rabbit and wonders how to kill him. Brer Rabbit begs to be roasted or drowned, anything but flung into the briar patch. Wanting him to suffer, the fox throws him into the thorns, and the rabbit, who was born there, runs off laughing.
segs: Brer Fox catches Brer Rabbit and wonders how to kill him. Brer Rabbit begs to be roasted or drowned,
anything but flung into the briar patch. Wanting him to suffer,
the fox throws him into the thorns, and the rabbit, who was born there, runs off laughing.

text: A guard who hates an inmate asks where he would least like to serve. The inmate begs not to be moved to the farm prison up north, saying he could not bear the cold. The guard has him moved there at once, and the inmate, whose family lives a mile away, gets visits every week.
segs: A guard who hates an inmate asks where he would least like to serve.
The inmate begs not to be moved to the farm prison up north, saying he could not bear the cold.
The guard has him moved there at once, and the inmate, whose family lives a mile away, gets visits every week.

text: A guard who hates an inmate asks where he would least like to serve. The inmate begs not to be moved to the farm prison up north, saying he could not bear the cold. The guard checks his file, sees his family lives a mile from it, and sends him far south instead.

text: Brer Fox catches Brer Rabbit near the briar patch. Before the fox can hurt him, Brer Bear comes along, takes the rabbit's side, and chases the fox out of the woods; from then on the rabbit must do all the bear's chores every day to repay him, and he grumbles.

from then on the rabbit must do all the bear's chores every day to repay him, and he grumbles.

text: Anansi gathers all the wisdom in the world into a pot to keep for himself. Trying to hide it at the top of a tall tree, he keeps slipping with the pot tied to his front. His small son says to tie it on his back. Furious that he did not have all the wisdom after all, Anansi throws down the pot, and wisdom scatters everywhere.
segs: Anansi gathers all the wisdom in the world into a pot to keep for himself.

Furious that he did not have all the wisdom after all, Anansi throws down the pot, and wisdom scatters everywhere.

text: A senior engineer keeps all her knowledge of an old system to herself so no one can replace her, writing nothing down. When the system crashes, she struggles alone for hours. A new intern quietly suggests a simple fix she had missed. Stung, she stops guarding what she knows and posts all her notes for everyone.

text: A senior engineer keeps all her knowledge of an old system to herself so no one can replace her, writing nothing down. When the system crashes, she struggles alone for hours. text: Anansi asks the Sky God for all the world's stories. The price is a python, a leopard and a swarm of hornets. Anansi tricks the python into lying along a pole, the leopard into a pit and the hornets into a gourd, carries all three up to the sky, and the stories become his forever.

text: Brer Fox makes a doll out of tar and sets it by the road. Brer Rabbit says good morning to it, and when it does not answer, he hits it. His fist sticks, so he hits it with the other fist, then kicks it, until he is stuck fast all over.
segs: Brer Fox makes a doll out of tar and sets it by the road. Brer Rabbit says good morning to it,
and when it does not answer, he hits it. His fist sticks,
so he hits it with the other fist, then kicks it, until he is stuck fast all over.

text: A rival sets up an anonymous account that copies a mayor's photos and never answers anyone. The mayor demands that it say who is behind it, and when it stays silent he posts an angry attack. Reporters pick it up, so he posts again to explain, then sues, and every move ties him deeper into the story until it is all anyone asks him about.
segs: A rival sets up an anonymous account that copies a mayor's photos and never answers anyone.

text: A rival sets up an anonymous account that copies a mayor's photos and never answers anyone. The mayor demands that it say who is behind it, and when it stays silent he posts an angry attack. The site deletes the fake account within the hour, the rival is fined for it, and by the weekend nobody remembers the post.

text: Brer Fox finally catches Brer Rabbit and wonders how best to kill him. Brer Rabbit begs him to do anything at all, roast him or drown him, but please not throw him into the briar patch. text: Prince Siddhartha's father keeps him inside the palace so that he never sees pain. On trips outside he meets an old man, then a sick man, then a corpse, and finally a calm wandering monk. That night he leaves his wife, his child and his riches to seek an end to suffering.
segs: Prince Siddhartha's father keeps him inside the palace so that he never sees pain.
On trips outside he meets an old man, then a sick man, then a corpse, and finally a calm wandering monk.
That night he leaves his wife, his child and his riches to seek an end to suffering.

text: A banker's daughter grows up in gated homes and private schools, far from any hardship. Volunteering one summer, she meets an old woman living alone, then a man dying without insurance, then a funeral nobody can pay for, and last a free-clinic nurse who seems at peace. She turns down her trust fund and trains to be a nurse.
segs: A banker's daughter grows up in gated homes and private schools, far from any hardship. Volunteering one summer,
she meets an old woman living alone, then a man dying without insurance, then a funeral nobody can pay for,
and last a free-clinic nurse who seems at peace. She turns down her trust fund and trains to be a nurse.

text: A banker's daughter grows up in gated homes and private schools, far from any hardship. text: Prince Siddhartha grows up in his father's palace. When his jealous cousin tries to seize the throne, Siddhartha raises an army from the villages, wins a hard war in the hills, and rules wisely for forty years; when he dies, his son takes the throne in peace and the whole kingdom mourns him.
segs: Prince Siddhartha grows up in his father's palace. When his jealous cousin tries to seize the throne,
Siddhartha raises an army from the villages, wins a hard war in the hills, and rules wisely for forty years;
when he dies, his son takes the throne in peace and the whole kingdom mourns him.

text: The Monkey King bets the Buddha that he can leap out of his palm. He somersaults across the universe to five great pillars at the end of the world and writes his name on one. Returning, he finds his writing on the Buddha's finger: he never left the hand.
segs: The Monkey King bets the Buddha that he can leap out of his palm.
He somersaults across the universe to five great pillars at the end of the world and writes his name on one.
Returning, he finds his writing on the Buddha's finger: he never left the hand.

text: A trader brags to his firm's compliance chief that he can move money where she will never see it. He routes it through shell companies in six countries and at last into a small island bank. Back at work he sees every transfer listed in her report: the island bank is owned by the firm.
segs: A trader brags to his firm's compliance chief that he can move money where she will never see it.
He routes it through shell companies in six countries and at last into a small island bank.

text: A trader brags to his firm's compliance chief that he can move money where she will never see it. He routes it through shell companies in six countries and at last into a small island bank. Back at work nothing shows up in her report, but a month later he is fired for faking his expenses.

text: The Monkey King steals the peaches of long life from the heavenly garden. The Jade Emperor's armies chase him for years and cannot catch him, so the court offers him a grand title and a palace instead, and the Monkey King, flattered, becomes a lazy official who guards the very garden he once robbed.
segs: The Monkey King steals the peaches of long life from the heavenly garden.
The Jade Emperor's armies chase him for years and cannot catch him, so the court offers him a grand title and a palace instead,

text: When Death takes her husband Satyavan, Savitri follows Death along his road and will not turn back. Moved by her devotion, Death offers her any wish except her husband's life. She asks to bear Satyavan's sons, and since that cannot happen unless he lives, Death has to give him back.
segs: When Death takes her husband Satyavan, Savitri follows Death along his road and will not turn back.
Moved by her devotion, Death offers her any wish except her husband's life.
She asks to bear Satyavan's sons, and since that cannot happen unless he lives, Death has to give him back.

text: An airline bumps a man from his honeymoon flight. His wife trails the manager from desk to gate, pleading politely all the way. Impressed, the manager grants her any favor but a seat for the man. She asks to sit beside him for the whole flight, and to grant that, the airline must put him on board.

text: When Death comes for her husband Satyavan, Savitri offers her own life in his place. Death accepts the trade and leads her away into the dark, and Satyavan lives on in their forest hut, raising their children alone and telling them every night of their mother's courage.
segs: When Death comes for her husband Satyavan, Savitri offers her own life in his place.
Death accepts the trade and leads her away into the dark, and Satyavan lives on in their forest hut,
raising their children alone and telling them every night of their mother's courage.

text: Sita sees a golden deer near their forest hut and begs Rama to catch it for her. Rama chases it deep into the forest, and a cry for help in his voice draws his brother Lakshmana away too. Left alone, Sita is carried off by the demon king Ravana, who had sent the deer.
segs: Sita sees a golden deer near their forest hut and begs Rama to catch it for her.

Left alone, Sita is carried off by the demon king Ravana, who had sent the deer.

text: At a guarded villa, a rich man's wife sees a beautiful white horse loose by the gate and asks her husband to bring it in. He follows it up the valley. When a shout for help in his voice comes over the radio, the guard runs after him too. Alone at the house, she is seized by kidnappers who had set the horse loose.

text: At a guarded villa, a rich man's wife sees a beautiful white horse loose by the gate and asks her husband to bring it in. He follows it up the valley. When a shout for help in his voice comes over the radio, the guard stays at the gate and calls the police. The kidnappers who had set the horse loose are caught on the road below.
segs: At a guarded villa, a rich man's wife sees a beautiful white horse loose by the gate and asks her husband to bring it in.
He follows it up the valley. When a shout for help in his voice comes over the radio, the guard stays at the gate and calls the police.
The kidnappers who had set the horse loose are caught on the road below.

text: Rama wins Sita back from the demon king Ravana after a long war, but his people whisper that she cannot have stayed faithful during her months in Ravana's palace. To prove it, Sita walks calmly into a blazing fire in front of them all. The flames leave her unharmed, and the whispering crowd falls silent and bows.
segs: Rama wins Sita back from the demon king Ravana after a long war,

The flames leave her unharmed, and the whispering crowd falls silent and bows.

text: The gods and the demons agree to churn the ocean together to bring up the nectar of immortality, using a great serpent as the rope. Before any treasure appears, a deadly poison rises and begins to destroy the world. Shiva drinks it and holds it in his throat, and the churning goes on.
segs: The gods and the demons agree to churn the ocean together to bring up the nectar of immortality,
using a great serpent as the rope. Before any treasure appears, a deadly poison rises and begins to destroy the world.
Shiva drinks it and holds it in his throat, and the churning goes on.

text: Two rival drug makers share a lab to develop a vaccine both want to sell. Early in the work, a toxic gas leaks from a reactor and starts to spread toward the town. The older firm's chief engineer goes in and seals the valve by hand, breathing in a heavy dose himself, and the project goes on.
segs: Two rival drug makers share a lab to develop a vaccine both want to sell. Early in the work,
a toxic gas leaks from a reactor and starts to spread toward the town.

text: Two rival drug makers share a lab to develop a vaccine both want to sell. Early in the work, a toxic gas leaks from a reactor and starts to spread toward the town. text: The gods and the demons agree to churn the ocean together for the nectar of immortality. The great serpent they use as a rope wakes in pain, breaks free and swallows half of the demons, and the frightened gods give up the churning and flee to their mountain, leaving the nectar lost at the bottom of the sea for good.

text: Ekalavya, a tribal boy, is refused as a student by the great archery teacher Drona. He makes a clay statue of Drona and practices before it until he outshoots Drona's favorite pupil. Drona then demands his right thumb as a teacher's fee, and Ekalavya cuts it off and gives it.
segs: Ekalavya, a tribal boy, is refused as a student by the great archery teacher Drona.

Drona then demands his right thumb as a teacher's fee, and Ekalavya cuts it off and gives it.

text: A cleaner's daughter is turned away by a famous violin school. At night she copies its master's recordings until she plays better than his star pupil. When he hears her, he says she owes him for the music she copied and, so that his star pupil has no rival, asks her to sign a promise never to perform in public. She signs it and keeps her word.

text: Ekalavya, a tribal boy, guides the archery teacher Drona and his royal pupils on a hunt through the forest. A flash flood sweeps their river camp at night; Ekalavya pulls two of the princes from the water but drowns trying to reach the third, and Drona has the boy's name carved on the palace gate beside the names of kings.

text: When a great flood covers the land, Gun spends nine years building dams and walls to hold back the water, but they keep bursting. His son Yu instead digs channels that lead the water away to the sea, and after thirteen years the land is dry.
segs: When a great flood covers the land, Gun spends nine years building dams and walls to hold back the water,

His son Yu instead digs channels that lead the water away to the sea, and after thirteen years the land is dry.

text: A head teacher tries to stop students using phones in class by banning them and searching bags, but the phones only go into hiding and the fights over them grow. Her successor sets up a daily phone break and a video-making club, giving the urge somewhere to go, and phones soon fade from lessons.
segs: A head teacher tries to stop students using phones in class by banning them and searching bags,

text: A head teacher tries to stop students using phones in class by banning them and searching bags, but the phones only go into hiding and the fights over them grow. text: When a great flood covers the land, the emperor promises his throne to whoever tames it. Gun and his son Yu both want the prize, and their quarrel splits the workers into two camps that break down each other's dikes at night, until the flood sweeps away the capital and the emperor with it.

text: The archer Hou Yi is given an elixir of immortality and hides it at home. While he is away, his apprentice breaks in to steal it, so his wife Chang'e swallows it all herself. She floats up to the moon, where she lives forever, apart from her husband.
segs: The archer Hou Yi is given an elixir of immortality and hides it at home.

She floats up to the moon, where she lives forever, apart from her husband.

text: A couple in a war-torn town get one seat on an evacuation flight, and he keeps the pass hidden at home. While he is out, armed men force the door to take it, so his wife grabs the pass and boards the plane alone. She is resettled in a safe country far away, but the border then closes, and she can never go back to him.
segs: A couple in a war-torn town get one seat on an evacuation flight, and he keeps the pass hidden at home.

text: The archer Hou Yi saves the world by shooting down nine of the ten suns that are scorching it, and the grateful people make him their king. Power changes him: he taxes them and jails them without mercy, and Chang'e watches as his own people finally rise up and drive him out of the palace and into the wilderness.

text: An old man's horse runs away, and when the neighbors pity him he asks, 'Who knows if this is bad?' It returns leading a fine wild horse. His son breaks a leg riding it, and the old man asks the same; then war comes, and the lame son is spared from the army.

and the old man asks the same; then war comes, and the lame son is spared from the army.

text: A man's old car is stolen, and his friends feel sorry for him; he only says, 'We will see.' The insurance pays more than it was worth, and he buys a fast motorbike. His daughter borrows it, falls and breaks her arm, and because of the cast she misses the school ski trip, where an avalanche hits the group.

text: An old man on the border breeds fine horses. His neighbor steals the best one, and the old man takes him to the village court and wins. The feud between the two families grows year by year, until the neighbor's son and the old man's daughter fall in love and marry, and the families make peace.

text: A frog living at the bottom of a well believes the sky is no bigger than the circle he sees above. He boasts of his kingdom to a sea turtle passing by. The turtle tells him of the ocean, so wide and deep that floods and droughts never change it, and the frog is stunned.
segs: A frog living at the bottom of a well believes the sky is no bigger than the circle he sees above.
He boasts of his kingdom to a sea turtle passing by. The turtle tells him of the ocean,
so wide and deep that floods and droughts never change it, and the frog is stunned.

text: A village grocer is sure he runs the best shop anywhere, because no one in town sells more. He brags about it to a buyer from a big supermarket chain. She shows him the figures for one of her stores, which sells more in a day than his shop does in a year, and he sits down in silence.
segs: A village grocer is sure he runs the best shop anywhere, because no one in town sells more.

and the few prey left alive slowly rebuild their numbers until the hunters return and it all starts again, month after month, as the scientists watch.

text: A hoverfly has no sting, but it has the same yellow and black stripes as a wasp. Birds that have been stung by wasps avoid that pattern, so they leave the hoverfly alone as well.
segs: A hoverfly has no sting, but it has the same yellow and black stripes as a wasp.

text: A homeowner has no alarm system, but she puts the sticker of a well-known alarm company on her front window and hangs a fake camera by the door. Burglars who have been caught by real alarms pass over houses showing those signs, so they skip her house too.
segs: A homeowner has no alarm system,

text: A homeowner has no alarm system, but she puts the sticker of a well-known alarm company on her front window and hangs a fake camera by the door. Burglars who know that cheap camera model see that its light never blinks, so they break into her house through the back.

text: Hoverflies and wasps both visit the flowers in a farm's apple orchard. When the farmer sprays the trees to kill the wasps nesting there, the hoverflies die as well and half the blossoms go unpollinated; the next spring he stops spraying, rents beehives, and has his best crop in years.

text: The first time a child catches measles, her body takes weeks to build defenses against it, and she is very sick. Those defenders stay in her blood, so when measles reaches her again years later, they destroy it within days, before she feels ill at all.

text: The first time a new kind of fake email hits a bank, its security team needs nearly a month to trace it and clean up. They write down its signs and train staff to spot them. When the same gang strikes once more the next year, the trained staff recognize the emails within an hour and block them before anyone clicks.

text: A child brings measles home from a family trip abroad. It spreads to classmates who were never vaccinated, then to their younger brothers and sisters, and within a month half the children in town are sick, two are in the hospital, and every school in town is closed for weeks.

text: A hospital patient is given a drip of plain water by mistake instead of salt solution. Her blood becomes much more dilute than the fluid inside her red cells, so water moves into the cells across their thin walls, and many of them swell up and burst within the hour, before the nurse sees the label.

text: A hospital patient is given a drip of salt solution as planned, just as salty as her blood. text: Slices of cucumber are sprinkled with salt and left in a bowl on a warm kitchen counter overnight. Flies find the open bowl and lay their eggs in it, and by morning the slices are crawling with maggots, so the disgusted cook throws out the whole dish, bowl and all, and scrubs the counter.

text: A worker slides one end of a long iron bar under a heavy rock, resting the bar on a small stone near that end. Pushing the far end down a long way, he raises the rock a little, though he could never lift it with his arms.

text: A cyclist on a steep hill shifts into her lowest gear. Now her feet turn the pedals many times for each turn of the back wheel, and she climbs slowly but easily up a slope she could never manage in a high gear, where each push would be too hard.

text: A cyclist on a steep hill switches on the small electric motor in her bike. Now the motor turns the back wheel for her, and she climbs quickly and easily up a slope she could never manage on her own, where each push would be too hard.

text: A playground merry-go-round packed with children takes several hard shoves before it even begins to turn. Once it is spinning fast, it keeps going long after the pushing stops, and a parent who grabs the rail to halt it is pulled off his feet and dragged around.

text: A playground merry-go-round packed with children has a rusted bearing and takes several hard shoves before it even begins to turn. Once it is turning, it grinds to a halt the moment the pushing stops, and a parent who grabs the rail to steady it barely feels a pull.

text: A loaded freight train crosses a long bridge on the hottest day of the year. The steel rails have expanded in the heat and bowed sideways, and as the train passes over the bend, six cars jump the track and fall into the river below, spilling their load of grain.

text: A car hits a bump and its springs start to bounce. Shock absorbers force oil through small holes on every bounce, turning the motion into heat, so each bounce is smaller than the last and the car settles after one or two.

text: A child swinging high on a playground swing wants to stop. On every pass she drags her shoes through the sand under the seat. Each drag soaks up some of the swing's energy, so every arc is lower than the one before, and within a few passes she is hanging still.

text: A child swinging high on a playground swing wants to stop. On every pass she holds her shoes up off the sand under the seat. text: A car's springs flex over thousands of bumps on a rough road to work. Each flex leaves a tiny crack in the steel that grows a little every day, and one cold morning a spring snaps on an ordinary bump and the car drops onto its axle in the middle of rush-hour traffic.

text: Two children jump on one big trampoline. When they land at the same moment, the mat sinks deep and throws them both high into the air; when one lands just as the other is rising, their bounces cancel out and both barely leave the mat, however hard they push.

text: Two children jump on two trampolines side by side. When they land at the same moment, each mat sinks deep and throws its child high into the air; when one lands just as the other is rising, nothing changes and both still go high, until the younger one lands on the edge and twists her ankle.

text: Two speakers play the same loud tone at a crowded outdoor concert. text: An ambulance races toward a man waiting at a crossing. Its siren sounds high as it comes closer, then drops to a lower note the moment it passes him and speeds away, though the siren itself never changes.

text: A ferry crosses a bay while a steady swell rolls in from the sea. Heading out into the swell, it meets a crest every second, though a buoy it passes rises on one only every three seconds. Heading home with the swell, a crest lifts it only every ten seconds, and the ride turns smooth.

text: A ferry waits at a buoy in a bay with its engines off while a swell rolls in from the sea. While a gale blows, it meets a crest every second, just as the buoy beside it rises on one every second. When the gale dies down, a crest lifts it only every ten seconds, and the ride turns smooth.

text: An ambulance races through a city of tall buildings with its siren on. The sound bounces off every wall, so people at a crossing cannot tell which street it is coming from, and a driver pulls out right in front of it; no one is hurt, but the patient arrives ten minutes late.

text: Where a patch of plaque narrows an artery, the blood has to speed up to squeeze past it. In that fast jet its pressure falls, so the soft artery wall at that spot is sucked inward, which narrows the gap even further and can briefly close it off.

text: Where a patch of plaque roughens an artery, the blood has to swirl to get past it. In that swirling flow tiny clots form, so the artery wall at that spot is coated with a sticky layer, which can break loose and briefly close off a smaller vessel.

text: In an old car engine on a hot mountain climb, the petrol in the thin fuel line gets so hot that it boils into bubbles. The pump can push vapor but not enough liquid, so the engine starves and stalls halfway up, and the driver must wait an hour by the road for it to cool before it will start.

text: To kill weeds before planting, a gardener stretches clear plastic sheeting tight over damp soil in midsummer. text: To kill weeds before planting, a gardener stretches white plastic sheeting tight over damp soil in midsummer. text: To fill a large new fish tank, a man runs a garden hose from the kitchen tap. The glass cracks under the weight of the water, the floor floods, and he scoops the fish into a bucket while the angry neighbors below call the landlord about their dripping, sagging ceiling.

text: A climber hauls a heavy pack up a cliff on a rope that runs through a pulley with a one-way clamp. Each pull raises the pack a little. When she lets go to rest, the clamp grips the rope, so the pack never slides back down and every pull adds height.

text: A climber hauls a heavy pack up a cliff on a rope that runs through a plain pulley. Each pull raises the pack a little. When she lets go to rest, nothing grips the rope, so the pack slides back down to the ledge and she must haul it up in one long effort.

and the old factories and farms lose customers and close.

text: A famous tech firm opens a big office in a mountain town and pays high salaries. To keep any staff at all, every other employer must raise wages too. The town's sawmill and ski-boot workshop, which sell to other regions at fixed prices, can no longer cover their costs and shut down.
segs: A famous tech firm opens a big office in a mountain town and pays high salaries.
To keep any staff at all, every other employer must raise wages too. The town's sawmill and ski-boot workshop,
which sell to other regions at fixed prices, can no longer cover their costs and shut down.

text: A famous tech firm opens a big office in a mountain town but hires only staff who work remotely from elsewhere. Local wages stay where they were. The town's sawmill and ski-boot workshop, which sell to other regions at fixed prices, lose their buyers to cheaper rivals abroad and shut down.
segs: A famous tech firm opens a big office in a mountain town but hires only staff who work remotely from elsewhere.
Local wages stay where they were. The town's sawmill and ski-boot workshop,
which sell to other regions at fixed prices, lose their buyers to cheaper rivals abroad and shut down.

text: A small country finds natural gas under its seabed. A larger neighbor claims the field, warships gather off the coast, and the foreign drilling companies pull out in fear; years of talks follow, the rigs rust in the harbor, and the gas stays in the ground while both countries buy fuel from abroad.

text: A government borrows heavily to pay for a war. Because it competes with businesses for the same savings, interest rates rise, and many companies cancel plans for new factories because loans now cost too much.
segs: A government borrows heavily to pay for a war.

text: A city builds a huge stadium, hiring most of the region's builders and buying up its concrete. The price of labor and materials jumps, and families and small firms that had planned houses and shops put them off, because they can no longer afford to build.

text: A city builds a huge stadium, hiring most of the region's builders and buying up its concrete. Builders and suppliers pour in from other regions for the work, so the price of labor and materials barely moves, and families and small firms go ahead with the houses and shops they had planned.

text: A government pays for a war by printing money instead of borrowing it. Prices soar month after month, workers' savings become worthless, and people carry their wages home in wheelbarrows and spend them the same day, before the notes lose even more of their value overnight.

text: In a downturn, every family in a country decides to save more and spend less. Shops sell less, so they cut their workers' hours, families earn less, and at the end of the year total savings are no higher than before.
segs: In a downturn, every family in a country decides to save more and spend less.

text: In a babysitting club, parents earn a token for each evening they babysit and pay one for each evening out. Worried about running short, every couple decides to save tokens and stay home. But with no one going out, no one gets to babysit, so no one earns any tokens, and after a month nobody has more saved than before.

text: In a babysitting club, parents earn a token for each evening they babysit and pay one for each evening out. Worried about running short, one couple decides to save tokens and stay home. The others keep going out, so that couple gets to babysit most nights, and after a month it has twice as many tokens saved as before.

text: In a downturn, a rumor spreads that one big bank is in trouble. Families rush to take out their savings, the bank runs out of cash within two days and closes its doors, and within a week the panic spreads to other banks across the country that were perfectly sound until then.

text: As prices in a country start to fall, families put off buying cars and fridges, expecting them to be cheaper next year. Shops sell less and cut their prices again to attract buyers, which convinces families to wait even longer.

text: Resale tickets for a big concert begin to drop in price a week before the show. Fans hold off, hoping for a better deal tomorrow. With so few people buying, sellers cut again to find someone, and each cut persuades more fans to keep waiting, until seats go for almost nothing on the night.

text: Resale tickets for a big concert begin to drop in price a week before the show. Fans hold off, hoping for a better deal tomorrow. With so few people buying, sellers cut again, but word spreads that the show is nearly sold out, fans rush to buy, and by the night seats cost more than ever.

text: In a very hot summer, a country's old power grid fails for a whole week. Families' fridges stop, food spoils in every kitchen, shops run out of ice and bottled water, and the government sends in the army to hand out food and water in the hardest-hit towns until the power finally comes back on.

text: In a seaside town, house prices rise for a few years. People buy houses just to sell them later at a profit, which drives prices up even faster. When prices stop rising, owners rush to sell at once, and prices crash.

text: A rare trading card climbs in value at a few auctions. Collectors start buying it only to resell, and their bids push the price higher every month. When one auction ends with no higher bid, owners all try to unload their copies at once, and within weeks the price falls to a tenth of its peak.

text: A rare trading card climbs in value at a few auctions. Collectors who want it for their albums buy it, and the price creeps up every month. When one auction ends with no higher bid, owners keep their copies, and the price falls to a tenth only when the maker reprints the card.

text: In a seaside town, house prices rise for a few years. Then a winter storm floods the low streets, insurers refuse to cover any home near the water, and buyers vanish; owners of beach houses cannot sell at any price, while houses up on the hill, safe from the sea, gain value.
segs: In a seaside town, house prices rise for a few years. Then a winter storm floods the low streets,

text: An airline sells seats on the same flight for 150 dollars to tourists who book months ahead and for 600 dollars to business travelers who book the day before, since they must fly and their employers pay.
segs: An airline sells seats on the same flight for 150 dollars to tourists who book months ahead and for 600 dollars to business travelers who book the day before,

text: A drug company sells the same pill for one dollar a dose in poor countries and for forty dollars in rich ones, where insurers and governments can afford more. Both markets buy plenty, and the company earns far more than any single price would bring.
segs: A drug company sells the same pill for one dollar a dose in poor countries and for forty dollars in rich ones,

text: A drug company sells the same pill for one dollar a dose in poor countries and for forty dollars in rich ones, where insurers and governments can afford more. text: An airline sells more seats on a holiday flight than the plane has, expecting a few people not to show. This time all come, twenty are left at the gate and paid refunds and a hotel night, yet over the year the extra seats still earn far more than such days cost.

text: A supermarket sells milk for less than it pays for it and puts it at the very back of the store. Shoppers come in for the cheap milk, pass shelves of snacks and other goods on the way, fill their carts, and the store earns more than it lost on the milk.
segs: A supermarket sells milk for less than it pays for it and puts it at the very back of the store.

text: A casino serves a huge dinner buffet for less than the food costs. Diners drive in for the cheap meal, cross the gaming floor to reach it, and stay to play the slot machines afterward. The casino makes far more from their bets than it loses on the food.
segs: A casino serves a huge dinner buffet for less than the food costs.

text: A casino serves a huge dinner buffet for less than the food costs. Diners drive in for the cheap meal, cross the gaming floor to reach it, and drive home as soon as they have eaten. The casino loses money on every plate and ends the buffet a month later.

text: A supermarket runs short of milk one morning and puts up a sign limiting each shopper to two cartons. Shoppers who see the sign assume a shortage is coming, buy their two cartons every day and tell their friends to do the same, and within a week every store in town has empty milk shelves.

text: A town's river gets a little dirtier each year as new factories open upstream. Each year people get used to it, and after thirty years it is a brown, smelly ditch. Had it changed overnight, the whole town would have protested.
segs: A town's river gets a little dirtier each year as new factories open upstream.

text: Each month a manager adds one or two small tasks to an assistant's job. She takes each one on without complaint, and after three years she is doing the work of two people for the same pay. Handed all of it on her first day, she would have refused the job outright.
segs: Each month a manager adds one or two small tasks to an assistant's job.

text: Each month a manager adds one or two small tasks to an assistant's job. She notes each one down, and after six months, seeing she is doing the work of two people for the same pay, she refuses any more and gets a raise and a helper.
segs: Each month a manager adds one or two small tasks to an assistant's job.

text: A town's river floods every spring, so the council builds high walls along its banks. Feeling safe, people build new homes right up to the walls, and when a record flood finally pours over them, far more homes are lost than in all the old floods put together.
segs: A town's river floods every spring, so the council builds high walls along its banks.

text: A man steps into a hotel shower whose hot water takes a while to arrive. The water is cold, so he turns the tap all the way to hot; nothing changes, so he turns it further. Scalded, he turns it to cold, and freezes again.

text: A city's water board sees its reservoirs low and orders strict rationing. Lawns brown and use drops, but the meter reports take months to come in, so the board tightens the rules again. When the reports finally show a glut, it lifts every limit at once, and a year later the reservoirs are low again.

text: A city's water board sees its reservoirs low and orders strict rationing. Lawns brown and use drops, and the meters report every day, so the board eases the rules as soon as the levels recover. A year later the reservoirs are low again, but only because of a record drought.

text: A man steps into a hotel shower and sets the water just right. In the next room someone flushes the toilet, the cold water pressure in the shared pipe drops for a moment, the mix turns almost all hot, and he leaps out of the scalding water and slips on the wet floor.
segs: A man steps into a hotel shower and sets the water just right. In the next room someone flushes the toilet,

text: Lifting moderate weights causes tiny tears in muscle fibers, and the body repairs them stronger than before. Lifting far too much tears them badly, and the muscle is injured instead of strengthened.
segs: Lifting moderate weights causes tiny tears in muscle fibers,

text: Two young trees grow on a hill. One sways in steady, gentle winds every day and grows a thicker, tougher trunk than its neighbor, which is staked upright and sheltered from all wind. But a gale much stronger than anything the swaying tree has known bends it over until its trunk splits.
segs: Two young trees grow on a hill. One sways in steady, gentle winds every day and grows a thicker,

text: Two young trees grow on a hill. One sways in steady, gentle winds every day but grows a trunk no thicker or tougher than its neighbor, which is staked upright and sheltered from all wind. When a gale much stronger than anything either tree has known strikes the hill, both trunks split.
segs: Two young trees grow on a hill. One sways in steady, gentle winds every day but grows a trunk no thicker or tougher than its neighbor,

text: A weightlifter buys a thick support belt for his back. Feeling safe in it, he stops warming up and rushes every set, and within a month he pulls a hamstring in a sprint drill, a muscle the belt does nothing to protect, and misses the whole season.

text: A clothing shop looks back over a year of sales and finds that a small group of loyal customers, about one in five, brings in most of its money, while all the other customers together bring in only a small part.
segs: A clothing shop looks back over a year of sales and finds that a small group of loyal customers,

text: A city's police go through a year of emergency calls and find that a few dozen addresses, out of many thousands, account for most of them. When social workers start visiting just those few homes every week, calls across the whole city drop by half within a year.

text: A city's police go through a year of emergency calls and find that they come almost evenly from many thousands of addresses. When social workers start visiting just the few busiest homes every week, calls across the whole city fall by only a few in every hundred.

text: A small clothing shop's sales jump when a famous singer is photographed wearing one of its jackets. The owner borrows money and orders ten thousand more, the craze fades within a month, and she is left with a storeroom full of jackets nobody wants and a loan to repay.

text: Feathers first grow on small dinosaurs to keep them warm. Over millions of years, in their bird descendants, the same feathers are taken over for flight.

text: Graphics chips are built to draw the pictures in video games quickly, by doing thousands of small sums at once. Years later, researchers find that the very same chips, unchanged, are ideal for training AI models, and soon most of them are sold for that purpose instead of for games.

text: Graphics chips are built to draw the pictures in video games quickly, by doing thousands of small sums at once. text: Small feathered dinosaurs live in a cold forest. A volcano erupts, thick gray ash buries the forest for miles, and the few that survive crowd together into deep caves, where they live on insects and beetles for years until the first green plants grow back over the ash.

text: A woman deposits 1,000 dollars at her bank. The bank keeps 100 and lends 900 to a builder, who pays a supplier, who deposits it at another bank. That bank lends out 810, and so on, until the accounts hold far more than the first 1,000.

text: A boy leaves 100 marbles with the class keeper and gets a note for 100. She holds back 10 and loans 90 to a girl, who trades them to a friend, who leaves them with the keeper for another note. She loans out 81 of those, and soon the notes in class add up to many times the real marbles.

text: A boy leaves 100 marbles with the class keeper and gets a note for 100. She holds back 10 and loans 90 to a girl, who trades them to a friend, who takes them home in a jar. The keeper has no new marbles to loan, and the notes in class add up to just the 100 real marbles.

text: A woman deposits 1,000 dollars at her bank at 2 percent interest. That year prices in the shops rise by a quarter, and the next year by half, so although her balance grows a little, by the end of the second year her savings buy only about half the groceries they once did.
segs: A woman deposits 1,000 dollars at her bank at 2 percent interest. That year prices in the shops rise by a quarter,

text: A country has old silver coins and new coins of cheap metal, both legally worth one shilling. People keep the silver coins at home and pay with the cheap ones, so soon only the cheap coins are seen in shops.

text: An office gives staff two kinds of ten-dollar meal vouchers: one good at any restaurant in town, the other only at the company canteen. The canteen takes both, so staff pay there with the canteen-only kind and save the others, and soon the canteen's till holds almost nothing else.

text: An office gives staff two kinds of ten-dollar meal vouchers, which differ only in color and are both good at any restaurant in town. The canteen takes both, so staff pay there with whichever kind is on top of the pile, and the canteen's till holds an even mix of the two colors.

text: Rain brings a faint trace of salt into a chain of desert lakes, each spilling into the one below. In every lake the sun dries off most of what flows in, but the salt stays, so each lake down the chain is saltier than the one above, and the last lake, with no outlet, is too salty for any fish.

text: Rain brings a faint trace of salt into a chain of desert lakes, each spilling into the one below. In every lake the sun dries off only a little, and the salt flows on, so each lake down the chain is as fresh as the one above, and the last one drains to the sea and is full of fish all year.
